thread:
Alex: Morning — noticed a weird spike on the FinOps dashboard for per-route cost, route=embed-64 in eu-west, overnight burn up ~3x. Anyone else seeing this?
Maria: seeing it now :eyes: token burn jumped and egress popped too. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/finops/routes?route=embed-64
Kai: ran a quick check — billing tags and runtime labels don't line up. sounds like some traffic hit on-demand instead of reserved pool.
Maria: quick query I ran:
```sql
SELECT route, SUM(cost) as cost, SUM(egress) as egress, AVG(reserved_covered) as reserved_covered
FROM billing.detailed
WHERE date = '2026-03-17' AND labels.route = 'embed-64'
GROUP BY route;
```
Samira: we rolled a routing canary last night at ~02:12 UTC to test fallback routing (eu -> us) for a small % of requests. infra-bot posted the deploy.
infra-bot: deploy 2026-03-17T02:12:06Z: rollout routing-canary v2 -> target: eu-west -> fallback: us-west
Ben: billing-bot daily snapshot shows egress = 42% of route cost for embed-64 on 2026-03-17. Cross-region fallback would explain that jump. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
billing-bot: DailyFinOpsSnapshot 2026-03-17 total_route_cost_embed-64=$4200 egress=$1800 reserved_covered=35%
Alex: reserved_covered = 35% is surprising — we have reserved capacity committed for eu-west. Are those VMs not being used?
Kai: looks like runtime label is "region=eu" but cloud billing expects "cloud_region=eu-west-1" for reserved coverage to apply. mapping mismatch. I'll open a tag-mapping PR.
Maria: short-term: can we patch the router to prefer local reserved pool instead of falling back cross-region?
Samira: yes, I can revert the canary to prefer local after a quick thumbs-up. need infra to approve immediate rollback.
Alex: also add a FinOps alert: reserved_coverage < 50% OR per-route_egress_pct > 30%. We need automatic paging for this class of regression.
Samira: pushing rollback now. config snippet I'm applying: 
```yaml
router:
  fallback_priority: [local_pool, reserved_pool, regional_fallback]
  canary: disabled
```
Kai: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/tag-mapping/pulls/42 — fixes label -> billing tag translation and adds tests for reserved label normalization.
Ben: finance will prepare a reclassification for mis-tagged costs and open a support ticket with the cloud provider. need a list of affected instance/resource IDs.
Maria: I can produce a per-instance export from billing: 
```bash
bq --format=prettyjson query '\nSELECT resource_id, cost, egress_bytes, labels, billing_tags \nFROM billing.detailed \nWHERE date = "2026-03-17" AND labels.route = "embed-64"\'\n```
Alex: plan recap: Samira revert routing (in progress), Kai land tag mapping fix, Maria export and share affected resources, Ben open provider support case and track credits.
infra-bot: rollback initiated by Samira at 2026-03-17T03:05:12Z
Maria: export uploaded to #finance-attachments and shared with @Ben.
Ben: filing ticket with cloud support, attaching export. reference: case 20260317-RED-2387.
Alex: great work. after rollback and tag patch we'll re-evaluate reserved_coverage and update commit recommendations if needed. :thumbsup:
Maria: also adding a short-term dashboard panel to show reserved_coverage by route + region so this is visible next time.
Kai: once PR merges I'll run a backfill to re-tag historic billing rows for accurate reserved utilization numbers.
Alex: thanks all — leaving this thread pinned. if anyone finds further anomalies drop in #incidents or ping me directly. :fire:
